the importance of subsistance production in five new EU members and its contribution to rural poverty.

subsistence agriculture remains important for a significant part of the rural population in the five countries studied, particularly in Romania and Bulgaria.
subsistence farming is a major contributor to the livelihoods of poor agricultural households in Bulgaria and Romania, but not in the other three countries.
, for the majority of agricultural households in Bulgaria, Hungary and Romania, the value of household production of food and other goods is of great importance.

subsistence agriculture is an important component of the rural economy in the new Member States, particularly in Bulgaria, Romania and Slovakia.
subsistence production is a key element of rural livelihoods, especially for poorer households.

the value of subsistance production to rural household incomes in the five countries studied is substantial.
